messages:
Maya R: Thinking out loud — we should prototype a per-request token-cost cap + probabilistic downgrade to cheaper model variants for our lowest tier customers. Goal: keep tail latency/responses up while cutting token spend. Anyone see obvious gotchas?

Sanjay P: Sounds reasonable. Are you imagining a strict cap that rejects, or a soft cap that tries cheaper variants first?

Maya R: Soft cap. Prefer degrade-first: try original model, if estimated token cost > cap then with X% probability use a cheaper variant. That keeps higher-quality hits occasionally.

Kevin L: Two knobs then: max_token_cost and fallback_probability. Also need region penalties (eu/asia cost multiplier) so cap isn't global. Quick sketch of config we could expose in API/console: 

```
{ "routing_policy": { "tiers": { "bronze": {"max_token_cost": 0.0002, "fallback_prob": 0.75, "region_penalties": {"eu": 1.08}}, "silver": {"max_token_cost": 0.0005, "fallback_prob": 0.20}}}}
```

Anya: Console UX notes: show live "expected savings" gauge for each customer when you change max_token_cost / fallback_prob. Also a histogram for observed fallback_rate and quality regression alerts (linked to eval prompts).

Maya R: Good call on quality regression links. We shouldn't force users to guess. Telemetry we need at minimum: tokens_consumed_by_tier, fallback_rate_by_model_variant, cost_saved_estimate, p50/p95 latency with and w/o fallback.

Sanjay P: Also add a metric for aborted requests due to strict caps (if we ever implement strict reject). We don't want silent 4xx surprises.

Kevin L: API debate: expose this as a declarative routing_policy (tenant-level config + per-request overrides) or only as runtime heuristic baked into runtime? I vote declarative — easier for auditing and console. But we need to be careful about config explosion.

Anya: UX-wise declarative + an "experiment" toggle works best. Default for existing tenants = off. New tenants = opt-in with conservative defaults. For experiments, surface a rollout slider (0-100%) that can gradually increase fallback_prob.

Maya R: +1 for rollout slider. We should also support probabilistic rollouts at the route level (e.g., for /chat vs /completion).

ops-bot: deploybot: canary deploy of "routing-degrade-v1" would be required for runtime change. Queueing job #823 scheduled if we have green on unit tests.

Sanjay P: One more implement detail — estimating token cost pre-run isn't exact. We'll need a cheap heuristic (prompt length * per-token-cost) + model multiplier. That heuristic must be consistent between routing decision and billing calculations so customers don't get surprised.

Kevin L: Agree. Also propose adding an "economy-score" in traces so downstream SRE and billing can attribute saved tokens. Example trace fields: economy_score, routed_variant, estimated_token_cost, actual_token_cost.

Anya: On console, provide a "what-if" panel: simulate a month of traffic under current vs proposed policy showing projected savings and estimated quality impact (based on eval sets).

Maya R: Action items:
- Kevin: prototype routing_policy JSON + runtime hooks for fallback (ETA 1 week)
- Sanjay: design sampling heuristic for estimated token cost + tests (ETA 1 week)
- Anya: mockups for console "savings" and rollout slider + what-if panel (ETA 1 week)
- I'll draft telemetry events and a proposed default for Bronze (max_token_cost=0.00025, fallback_prob=0.6) and post here.

Kevin L: One API example for per-request override we could accept (for partners):
```
POST /v1/predict
{ "model": "redwood-v1", "prompt": "...", "routing": {"allowFallback": true, "budgetTokenCost": 0.0003} }
```

Maya R: Nice. We'll make sure per-request overrides are rate-limited and require explicit permission (partners only).

Sanjay P: Sounds good. If anyone objects to the plan, speak now. Otherwise I'll open an RFC with the config shape and telemetry schema today. :thumbsup:

Anya: No objections. +1 :chart_with_downwards_trend: for cost savings.

Maya R: Thanks team — will follow up with the RFC and a small spike branch.

ops-bot: ci-bot: tests passed on spike-branch (build 4821).
